One HTML is the checkpoint record

Open docs/checkpoints.html in a browser, including by double-clicking it. Charts, values, validation, instructions and historical report text are embedded. It needs no server, CDN, installation or network access. Browser filters do not edit the saved measurements.

Add the next checkpoint

  1. Measure a concrete source state. Record the commit, whether the working tree was dirty, source/executable hashes, date and timezone. If only the date survives in old evidence, preserve that precision.
  2. Keep conditions explicit. Reuse a protocol only when its workload, units, endpoint, hardware, sampling and aggregation are compatible. Use a new session ID for each measurement session and a new protocol/environment ID when conditions change.
  3. Keep the raw evidence. Store CSVs, JSON summaries, hashes and validation output in docs/evidence/<session>/. Run both binaries before measuring, discard warmups, verify equivalent output and preserve regressions as well as improvements.
  4. Fill a JSON bundle, then append it. The helper validates all observations before atomically updating the embedded data. Do not rewrite historical observations or generate another performance report as the primary record.
python scripts/checkpoints.py --template "$env:LOCALAPPDATA/Codex/tools/scratch/checkpoint.json"
# Fill the generated bundle with measured values and evidence.
python scripts/checkpoints.py --append "$env:LOCALAPPDATA/Codex/tools/scratch/checkpoint.json"
python scripts/checkpoints.py --check
python tests/benchmark/test_checkpoints.py
# For chart changes, also run (requires Node.js):
node tests/benchmark/test_checkpoint_charts.cjs
git diff --check

Commands run from the repository root in PowerShell. Create the scratch parent directory if needed. Use --list to find checkpoint IDs and --export <new-file.json> to inspect existing metrics, references, protocols and environments. --html <path> selects a different copy of the dashboard.

Bundle shape

The top level contains checkpoints and optionally new metrics, protocols, environments, references, historySeries and reports. Existing definitions cannot be redefined by the append command. Each checkpoint records:

FieldMeaning
id / labelUnique stable ID and human-readable change.
measuredAtISO 8601 timestamp with offset, or date only if the exact time is unknown.
commit / dirty / sourceNoteMeasured revision, dirty flag and source/build identity. Unknowns use null with an explicit explanation.
pairedWithOptional provenance for an original controlled source comparison; the dashboard displays history.
results[]Metric, protocol, environment, workload, session, value, sample count and raw evidence path.
tests[]Name, pass/fail/partial/not-run, passed/total, durationSeconds and evidence. Counts are the original run's scope.
notesChanges, test bounds, caveats and tradeoffs. Keep this useful without a separate report.

One current VLC reference

The timeline connects dated Aperture observations; VLC is a single fixed benchmark from the latest recorded version. Its newest available matching metric/workload/environment measurement is used across the history, with the actual reference date preserved. Older VLC runs stay in the evidence and never become a second timeline. Add new references entries with player, version, measuredAt and results. Optional result reference links preserve original same-session provenance and must still match all conditions. Never present an old run as newly measured. Internal benchmarks without a VLC equivalent remain empty.

Units & comparison rules

Record effective scaling options. Historical all-linear playback measurements use a faster picture-processing profile; they do not establish equal quality or predict the balanced app candidate. The balanced candidate keeps Lanczos/Hermite luma scaling and downsampling antialiasing, with bilinear chroma and no extra linear-light/sigmoid passes. Give different filter profiles separate protocol/workload identities.

  • All graph values use the metric definition's unit. MiB = 1,048,576 bytes. Recorded CPU values and history graphs use percent of one logical processor, so values may exceed 100. When the environment records its logical-processor count, the CPU summary card divides by that count and labels the result total capacity; its difference from VLC is in percentage points (pp). The original per-processor values remain in Measurements and the history. A +501% relative ratio is approximately 0.92% vs 0.15% of a 24-processor machine, not 501% total CPU. Counters for requested C++ heap bytes are separate from process private bytes and working set.
  • Delta is (current − baseline) / baseline × 100. Lower-is-better decreases are green; increases are red. These colors describe measured differences, not proof of a causal regression. Read run ranges and measurement reviews before attributing changes to code. A zero baseline produces no percentage; a missing value is never converted to zero.
  • Visible-window latency, GPU-shell latency, engine readiness and first video frame are different endpoints. Do not merge them. Runtime files are logical supplied bytes, not compressed download size.
  • Use value: null with missingReason for unavailable counters. Unknown sample counts need samplingNote. Keep failed verification out of successful playback measurements and record it in tests/notes.
  • Timeline stops follow measurement-date order with categorical checkpoint spacing, not invented elapsed times. The resource-map arrows follow the same chronological order. Cuts compresses empty numeric ranges and marks each omitted interval with an axis break; units remain linear within retained bands. Cuts apply to both resource axes and the timeline value axis. Linear and log modes remain available.
  • Reuse strict metric/protocol/workload/environment identities for a continuing series. A declared historySeries may join documented historical protocols only: define its label, method, exact workload and allowed protocols; assign its ID to each result. Metrics remain separate. Preserve differences in sampling or machine identity in provenance. The empty-profile startup group includes seven recordings; its first is a single sample and later gates use five-run medians. Per-result measuredAt can preserve an exact capture time.

Reproduce the measurements

For matched player runs, use -VideoWidth 1280 -VideoHeight 720 -ForceD3D11Linear and retain child-window dimensions/DPI and effective scaling settings. Equal outer windows do not imply equal video areas. Keep raw CPU time and cycle counters. A cycle-derived CPU estimate requires a supported result from calibrate_cpu_cycles.cpp on the same CPU/boot: invariant TSC, stable measured rate and busy-counter validation. Record the calibration, label the value as a hardware-specific estimate and use a separate protocol. Never substitute advertised MHz or rewrite historical CPU measurements.

Use the existing local runners in tests/benchmark/README.md, tests/backend/README.md, tests/loading/README.md and docs/TESTING.md. Player resource runs use compare_players.ps1; engine experiments use compare_playback_resources.ps1; capture probes use run_save_benchmark.ps1. Keep builds out of timed runs. Follow the local build/release policy; this dashboard does not run benchmarks itself.

Finish the update

Open the HTML, select the new checkpoint, inspect its comparisons and evidence, run the helper check and focused tests, then commit only the intended dashboard/evidence changes. The report library is a historical snapshot; future checkpoints belong in this record. Export buttons download copies without changing the source HTML.
